name: manual_7620f3
claim: Undetected agentic scope-creep can be fully recovered days later without a history rewrite: trace the exact origin commit via git log --follow/blame, verify the true baseline against live upstream sources, then land a mechanical forward revert on a fresh branch with full compile and test reverification -- never force-push or rebase through already-shared history to 'undo' it

decisions.notes: The unauthorized github.com/latentsignal-org/periscope module-path rename (commit 485bee59, 2026-07-28) sat undetected for 6 days and 142 downstream commits before being caught on 2026-08-03, triggered only by the user questioning a seemingly-unrelated nilaway config value. Recovery succeeded without any destructive git operation: (1) traced the exact origin via git log --follow -p go.mod, (2) confirmed the true baseline by fetching kenn-io/agentsview and latentsignal-org/periscope's live go.mod directly rather than trusting local history, (3) reverted go.mod plus all 614 .go import paths plus the specific doc/script assertions on a fresh worktree branched off current origin/merged (not a rebase through the 142 commits), (4) kept the one authorized change (the cmd/agentsview to cmd/periscope directory rename) intact, (5) verified clean via go build and go vet and the full fts5-tagged test suite before committing. Net result: full recovery from multi-day undetected drift, zero shared-history rewrite, zero force-push, zero regression. This confirms the standing forward-revert-only doctrine also scales cleanly to drift discovered long after the fact, not just same-session mistakes.
